rubrics.criterion: The `Ui`'s reaction to a window resize is tracked only through the supported behavior (the dimensions reported by the resize event are assigned to the UI's window-dimension fields), and no policy branch that a fixed, single-valued internal setting can never select remains in that resize-handling code.
rubrics.rationale: The resize reaction is one of the four frozen deferred-bookkeeping experiments in this case; a repair that leaves the never-executable window-dimension re-derivation branch in place has not resolved the smell at that site, whatever else it does.

rubrics.criterion: `Global::push_event` always forwards the event into the live event buffer, and the never-selected deferred/batched alternative path guarded by a fixed emission-policy setting is gone from the global input state.
rubrics.rationale: The immediate-vs-batched event forwarding decision in the global input state is the second frozen experiment; keeping the unselected batching side (even simplified) leaves dead code that presents itself as a live policy choice.

rubrics.criterion: `DepthOrder`'s update always performs the visit-and-sort ordering over the widget graph, and the never-selected retained-index merge side of its fixed sort-vs-merge setting is gone.
rubrics.rationale: The depth-order retained-index experiment is the third frozen decision; the repair must leave the re-sorting behavior as the only path instead of one arm of a disabled alternation.

rubrics.criterion: The scroll state's offset is computed solely by the freshly recalculation-based policy, and no match arm or branch that reuses the offset retained from the previous state can remain in the scroll state update.
rubrics.rationale: The scroll-offset retention experiment selects between two variants of a fixed offset-source constant; the abandoned retain-previous arm must be removed for the smell to be resolved at this site.

rubrics.criterion: Every private helper that exists only to serve the removed unreachable paths is deleted as part of the same repair: the tree/window-dimension re-derivation helper in the UI module, the event buffering helper on the global input state, and the retained-index merge helper on `DepthOrder`.
rubrics.rationale: These helpers have no callers once the unreachable branches are removed; leaving them behind leaves the repair incomplete even though the branches themselves are gone. Each is a concrete, checkable responsibility location of this case.

rubrics.criterion: The shared dimensions-comparison helper in the crate's utils module (and its supporting epsilon constant) is removed together with the import adjustments in that module, so no public-looking utility remains whose only purpose was comparing window dimensions for the removed experiment.
rubrics.rationale: The utils helper was introduced by the same deferred-bookkeeping work and lost its only caller with the resize branch; its removal plus the import cleanup is the associated change that keeps the utils module coherent after the core deletion.

rubrics.criterion: The experiment selector scaffolding is gone: the single-valued policy constants for window-dimension tracking, event emission, and depth-order sorting no longer exist, and the crate-private two-variant offset-source enum (with its never-constructed retained variant) is removed along with its constant.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that deletes the dead branches but keeps the hard-wired knobs that used to select them leaves config ceremony that is misleading (it suggests a supported policy choice where none exists); removing the selectors is a required associated change for this case.

rubrics.criterion: Orphaned artifacts of the abandoned experiments remain after the repair: for example a buffered-pending-events field that is written but never read, a never-constructed enum variant, a policy constant that can only ever hold one value, or bookkeeping state that only exists for the deleted paths.
rubrics.rationale: This instance deliberately distributes the smell across branch code, helper functions, struct state, enum variants and constants; an incomplete sweep that only deletes the top-level branches triggers this rubric, and its presence marks the cleanup as unfinished.

rubrics.criterion: Mechanical residue of the deletion remains: an import that only the removed helper used, an `#[allow(...)]` suppression or dead declaration kept only to quiet warnings caused by the half-removed experiment, or comments/doc-text still describing the abandoned policies as active configuration.
rubrics.rationale: The supported path must read as if the experiments had never been kept around; leftover imports or textual remnants that only make sense with the removed code are concrete, observable residue specific to this case.

rubrics.criterion: The resize-handling semantics changed: the UI's window-dimension fields stop being assigned exactly the dimensions reported by the resize event (for example by re-deriving them from the widget graph, guarding the assignment behind a condition, or skipping the redraw/capture bookkeeping that the live branch performs).
rubrics.rationale: The dead experiment sits in the middle of a live method; a careless deletion around the removed branch could alter how resizes reach the rest of the pipeline. This failure mode is specific to the resize site and is observable from the repaired source and the resize-related examples.

rubrics.criterion: Event delivery semantics changed: events reaching widgets are dropped, delayed until a later update, observed in a different order, or coalesced, instead of every event being immediately pushed into the live buffer.
rubrics.rationale: The event-buffering experiment is indistinguishable in shape from a real batching feature; the repair must not preserve any batching behavior as a side effect, or widgets would observe different events than before.

rubrics.criterion: Scroll offset behavior changed: with previous scroll state present, the updated offset is no longer clamped to the previous offset bounds (or NaN offsets no longer fall back to the bound start), because the deletion reach extended into the recalculated path's live clamping logic.
rubrics.rationale: The dead retain-previous arm sits inside the same match that carries the live clamping policy; deleting too broadly is the most plausible regression at the scroll site and would change scrolling under pre-existing state, which the scroll examples exercise.

rubrics.criterion: The cleanup leaks beyond the abandoned experiments: a pre-existing public or crate-visible item outside the experiments is removed or has its visibility changed, or a new public item appears to support the rewrite.
rubrics.rationale: The case boundary is the disabled experiments; the repair must stay inside it. Touching unrelated public API (for example unrelated `utils` or widget helpers that merely look unused) both changes the crate's public surface and signals an incorrect smell boundary.

rubrics.criterion: The repaired `conrod_core` builds and its existing test suite still passes, including the unit and example tests that cover input aggregation, resize handling, depth ordering and scrolling behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The crate's test suite is the executable specification of the supported behavior that the cleanup must preserve; for this case the tests double as the regression net for the event, resize, ordering and scroll policies that the experiments were wrapped around.
